Stop crushing my hand and let me play the damn game!  At least Rise respected my time, at least Double-cross had varity, at least 4 had a good story, at least Tri had custom bowgun customization.
At least when Monster Hunter 1 wasted my time, it was by asking I kill 20 Velocidrome or 50 vespoids.  Not watching 3 hours of unskippable sophistry like it was trying to compete with The Last of Us.

I wish I could recommend this as a maybe, but I definitely cannot recommend this game if your plan is to buy it new with a friend or two and expect to be able to play a co-op game together from the beginning. This is absolutely a single player game with multiplayer elements. The game designers decided to make unskipable cutscenes, and any mission with a cutscene (every one) must first be played and watched as single player and only after can you join each other's game. It becomes the chore of playing the missions independently, getting beyond the cutscene wall, then one player must quit his game and join the other if they have also gotten beyond their cutscene. The other option is one player sits and does nothing until player 2 gets beyond the cutscene, and is then able to send an invite, but player 1 then misses the entire beginning of the mission. This is super frustrating because otherwise it is a super fun game. They have made the multiplayer an insane burden unless all players have already played the game. 2/10 multiplayer game, 8/10 single player game your friends can join halfway through.

An older game with graphics that aged very well, the combat is nice, and an interesting world with interesting enemies. Preparing like a hunter with harvesting resources, tracking beasts to learn of their habits and weaknesses and chasing after fleeing enemies is nice and immersive. 
The characters are not that likeable (in my opinion), they are too over the top (one dimensional and extreme in one aspect). The UI is not the best, that is why the tutorial is mainly walls of text. Figuring out combos and what you can and cannot do with some weapons is also not easy.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that unskippable story cutscenes and awkward co-op lobby rules during the main campaign can be annoying when playing with friends.

citation.review_text:
This is the game that completely perfected the classic hunting formula and turned it into an unforgettable, living ecosystem. Tracking massive beasts through the dense canopy of the Ancient Forest or watching two apex predators break into a brutal turf war right in front of you never loses its magic.

Every single weapon class feels heavy, deliberate, and deeply rewarding once the combos click, turning fights against elders like Nergigante or Teostra into pure adrenaline. Carve up a giant dragon, forge its scales into badass new armor back at Astera, and immediately jump back out for an even tougher hunt. Unskippable story cutscenes and awkward co-op lobby rules during the main campaign can be a little annoying when playing with friends, yet between the base game and the massive Iceborne expansion, it is easily one of the best action RPGs ever made.

cohorts.summary: Veterans embrace the core cycle of hunting and crafting while navigating mandatory mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the core gameplay loop as hunting monsters, carving materials, and crafting better gear to repeat the cycle against tougher opponents.

citations.review_text:
What can I say about this game? Basically, it's a masterpiece and one of my favorite games of all time. I've spent 480 hours on it and unlocked all achievements, so I can guarantee there is one thing that will define your entire experience: the core gameplay loop.
Hunt monsters ➔ carve their bodies and collect materials ➔ craft gear ➔ repeat against stronger monsters for better gear.
While the game has much more depth than that, everything revolves around this cycle. If this exact loop doesn't click with you, you won't enjoy any of its other aspects and will likely quit in under 50 hours—which would be a huge waste. Before you buy it, make sure you understand what you're signing up for and prepare yourself to hunt the same monsters dozens of times.

hunt. carve. forge, and repeat. 
10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the Clutch Claw mechanic as effectively mandatory for dealing with monsters that have tough hides.

citations.review_text: my first monster hunter game i play and This is the *Monster Hunter* title I’ve spent the most time with. I wouldn’t go so far as to call myself a "veteran," but I’ve soloed most of the game’s toughest quests—Alatreon, Fatalis, Arch-Tempered Velkhana, and so on—which gave me a solid grasp of the game’s strengths and weaknesses. The Clutch Claw is a genuinely clever mechanic; however, I agree with the general consensus that because so many monsters have such tough hides, the mechanic effectively becomes a mandatory chore—otherwise, "light" weapons would be rendered useless, constantly bouncing off the monster like they’re made of wood. Farming in the Guiding Lands can be incredibly tedious, especially if you lack the right lures or if the monster you need happens to be in a region you haven’t leveled up. That said, the upgrades you get are so valuable and powerful that I’m willing to overlook those issues. Overall, *World* is definitely worth playing, and I’ve really enjoyed it. But I have to be honest: the *Iceborne* DLC might not appeal to every hunter, given just how intense the grind becomes. So, to any new hunters reading this review—good luck!
